work_items.title: Objective — Prove a portable agent-work handoff without a hosted dependency
work_items.outcome: Within 30–45 days, another person can capture a Codex or Claude coding session, create a signed Git-linked archive, verify it offline, and resume the task in the other agent without copying the original transcript.
work_items.journey: A person starts with a seeded Git task, works in one supported agent through Entire, creates and transfers an Open Work Commons archive, verifies it on a clean machine, prepares a bounded resume bundle, and completes the task in the other agent.
scope: Entire 0.9 or later as the first replaceable capture provider.
Codex → Claude and Claude → Codex handoffs.
Local identity, signed archive, exact Git binding, offline verification, and bounded resume bundle.
macOS ARM64 and Linux x86_64 installation evidence.
acceptance: Both handoff directions complete the seeded task and pass its predefined tests.
Verification requires no network or vendor account.
Every tested archive mutation fails non-zero and identifies the affected object.
Raw transcripts are excluded by default and hidden chain-of-thought is never requested.
The archive remains intelligible and verifiable without Entire.
non_goals: Multiplayer CRDT collaboration or a DeltaDB replacement.
Team synchronization, federation, hosted accounts, web UI, or orchestration.
Replacing Entire capture before a concrete sovereignty or compatibility failure exists.
evidence: Two seeded handoff recordings and acceptance-test results.
Release artifacts, checksums, SBOM, and clean-machine quickstart transcript.

work_items.title: Freeze v0 sovereignty, trust, privacy, and threat contract
work_items.outcome: One reviewed contract states exactly what v0 records, signs, exports, trusts, redacts, retains, and refuses to capture.
work_items.journey: A contributor can read one bounded RFC and threat model before implementing or reviewing any capture or archive behavior.
scope: Actor, session, checkpoint, artifact, claim, evidence, archive, and signer vocabulary.
Signature-valid versus signer-trusted distinction.
Secret leakage, malicious captured content, archive tampering, key loss, retention, and deletion.
Provider replacement and offline-continuity requirements.
acceptance: The v0 commands, supported platforms, authority boundaries, and non-goals are explicit.
Raw transcripts are off by default and hidden chain-of-thought is prohibited.
Redaction is required before durable storage.
Each named threat has a mitigation, accepted risk, or release-blocking disposition.
non_goals: Choosing a full team identity, federation, or CRDT architecture.
evidence: Reviewed RFC and threat model with recorded decisions for keys, canonicalization, redaction, and archive boundaries.

work_items.title: Establish the open-source repository and release baseline
work_items.outcome: Contributors can clone one clean repository, run one documented check, and inspect its mission, license, security policy, and contribution rules.
work_items.journey: A new contributor clones the repository, installs pinned dependencies, runs the checks, and can submit a change without founder-only knowledge.
scope: Apache-2.0 client, schemas, SDK, adapters, and conformance code.
DCO-style contribution policy without copyright assignment.
Pinned CI, formatting, type checking, tests, dependency review, SBOM, and signed-release plan.
acceptance: A clean checkout passes the documented check command.
Repository files contain no unrelated private-product data, private Plane identifiers, secrets, or copied unlicensed specifications.
Security reporting and release provenance expectations are documented.
Root configuration names Entire only as a replaceable adapter.
non_goals: Publishing a hosted service or creating a formal foundation in v0.
evidence: Clean-install CI run, license scan, secret scan, and repository tree review.

work_items.title: Create the seeded cross-agent handoff benchmark
work_items.outcome: One public synthetic repository task can measure whether a resume bundle improves a fresh agent handoff.
work_items.journey: An evaluator interrupts the seeded task at a fixed point, resumes with or without a bundle, and compares completion against the same acceptance tests.
scope: One deterministic task with hidden acceptance tests and an explicit interruption point.
Codex-first and Claude-first runs.
Time or tokens to first correct action, repeated questions, missed constraints, completion, and review effort.
acceptance: The task is solvable by either agent from the original issue and repository.
Baseline and bundle-assisted conditions differ only by the resume artifact.
The fixture contains no private code, credentials, or personal data.
Results can falsify the value of the bundle.
non_goals: Claiming general agent superiority from one task.
evidence: Seed repository, fixed interruption checkpoint, acceptance tests, scoring script, and baseline run record.

work_items.title: Publish v0 schemas and independent conformance fixtures
work_items.outcome: A second implementation can create and validate v0 records without importing the reference CLI.
work_items.journey: An implementer reads the schemas, validates golden fixtures, rejects malicious fixtures, and reproduces the recorded normative digests.
scope: Event, session, artifact, Git state, checkpoint, evidence, archive manifest, and resume-bundle schemas.
Canonical serialization and digest/signature inputs.
Valid, invalid, malicious, and version-migration fixtures.
acceptance: Every normative object has an explicit schema version.
Equal normative inputs reproduce the published digest.
Unknown extensions remain namespaced and cannot change core semantics.
A validator independent of application code passes the valid corpus and rejects the invalid corpus.
non_goals: A universal ontology for every work, life, or civic domain.
evidence: Published schemas, fixture corpus, recorded digests, and conformance output.

work_items.title: Build the local identity, event, and artifact store
work_items.outcome: The CLI initializes a private offline workspace that stores signed events and content-addressed artifacts without a hosted account.
work_items.journey: A person runs `owc init`, inspects the signer fingerprint and storage health, records events, restarts, and reads the same verified state offline.
scope: One local device identity.
OS key store or documented mode-0600 fallback.
Append-only events, content-addressed blobs, redaction before persistence, and `owc doctor`.
acceptance: Initialization and all reads work with network access disabled.
Secret canaries never appear in the store, blobs, logs, or exported fixtures.
Interrupted writes cannot corrupt previously committed records.
Doctor reports permissions, key health, schema version, and repair guidance.
non_goals: Multi-user synchronization, recovery ceremonies, or hosted identity.
evidence: Persistence, crash-recovery, permission, and secret-canary test output.

work_items.title: Bind checkpoints to exact Git state
work_items.outcome: A checkpoint identifies precisely which repository state it describes, including an uncommitted working tree.
work_items.journey: A person checkpoints clean, dirty, and divergent repositories and verifies each binding without contacting a remote.
scope: Repository identity, base and head commits, tree digest, dirty patch, and untracked-file manifest.
Clean, committed, dirty, and divergent fixture repositories.
acceptance: Checkpoint creation fails closed outside Git or for unresolved revisions.
Verification detects commit, tree, patch, and untracked-manifest changes.
No network lookup is required.
Sensitive ignored files are never included implicitly.
non_goals: Replacing Git or implementing live collaborative version control.
evidence: Git fixture repositories and binding/tamper integration-test output.

work_items.title: Use Entire as the first capture provider for Codex and Claude
work_items.outcome: The CLI imports supported Entire checkpoints for Codex and Claude into provider-neutral session events without requiring Entire.io login.
work_items.journey: A person enables Entire locally, runs either agent, selects a checkpoint, and sees which fields were imported, excluded, or unavailable before archive creation.
scope: Entire CLI 0.9 or later local checkpoint inspection.
Codex and Claude capture paths supported by Entire.
A provider capability report and explicit mapping to the v0 session schema.
An exit fixture proving the archive remains usable when Entire is absent.
acceptance: No Entire.io authentication or hosted API is required.
Raw transcripts are excluded unless a separate explicit policy enables them.
Unsupported and unavailable observations remain explicit rather than inferred.
Adapter failure cannot modify the Git worktree or corrupt the local store.
Fixture tests cover both agent types and a missing/incompatible Entire binary.
non_goals: Forking or replacing the MIT-licensed Entire CLI during v0.
evidence: Sanitized provider fixtures, capability output, mapping tests, and live local smoke records for Codex and Claude.

work_items.title: Compile and sign portable checkpoint archives
work_items.outcome: One command creates a self-contained signed archive that can be copied to another machine.
work_items.journey: A person selects an objective and Entire checkpoint, creates an archive, inspects its included and excluded objects, and copies the single artifact elsewhere.
scope: Objective, session range, Git state, artifacts, evidence, open questions, parent checkpoints, exclusions, and signer public identity.
Digest-addressed objects and deterministic root payload digest.
acceptance: Equal logical inputs produce the same root payload digest.
The private signing key never enters the archive.
Excluded raw or sensitive material is absent.
Round-trip export and import preserve every normative ID and digest.
Object removal, mutation, and substitution are detectable.
non_goals: Proving that every signed claim is factually true.
evidence: Golden archive, root digest, round-trip output, and mutation test matrix.

work_items.title: Verify archives fully offline and detect tampering
work_items.outcome: A clean disconnected machine validates an archive and distinguishes integrity from trust.
work_items.journey: A recipient copies an untrusted archive onto a disconnected machine, safely inspects it, verifies it against an optional trusted fingerprint, and receives actionable errors for mutations.
scope: Schemas, digests, signatures, parent graph, Git bindings, evidence subject digests, and explicit signer trust.
Safe inspection of malicious, oversized, and malformed archives.
acceptance: Verification performs no DNS, registry, API, or model access.
Integrity-valid and signer-trusted are reported separately.
Every tamper fixture fails non-zero and names the invalid object.
Inspection does not execute archive content or write outside its destination.
non_goals: Online identity attestation or centralized certificate authority.
evidence: Network-disabled verification transcript and complete tamper corpus with expected errors.

work_items.title: Compile bounded, cited cross-agent resume bundles
work_items.outcome: A verified archive produces a bounded resume bundle that either supported agent can consume without the original transcript.
work_items.journey: A recipient verifies an archive, chooses Codex or Claude and a size budget, reviews the generated bundle, and supplies it to the target agent.
scope: Machine-readable JSON and human-readable Markdown.
Objective, constraints, decisions, exact Git state, changes, evidence, gaps, next action, citations, exclusions, and untrusted-content delimiters.
acceptance: Every decisive statement references an archive object.
The configured byte/item budget is never exceeded.
Untrusted captured content is visibly and structurally delimited.
Bundle creation performs no agent launch or tool execution.
Codex and Claude consume golden bundles without transcript copying.
non_goals: Automatic orchestration or deciding the next task on the person's behalf.
evidence: Golden JSON/Markdown bundles, citation-integrity tests, budget tests, and seeded smoke records.

work_items.title: Prove Codex → Claude and Claude → Codex handoffs
work_items.outcome: Reproducible evidence shows whether the v0 handoff promise works and whether the bundle improves the seeded task.
work_items.journey: An evaluator runs both baseline and capsule-assisted handoffs in each direction, then compares acceptance, efficiency, questions, and missed constraints.
scope: One Codex → Claude and one Claude → Codex interrupted-task handoff.
Baseline equivalents using only the issue and repository.
Malicious content, secret canaries, oversized input, and archive tampering.
acceptance: The receiving agent receives the repository and bundle, not the original transcript.
Both assisted tasks pass their predefined acceptance tests.
The report records time or tokens to first correct action, repeated questions, missed constraints, completion, and review effort.
No unresolved critical security defect remains.
A null or negative result is reported without changing the metric after the run.
non_goals: Generalizing from one fixture to all agents or all forms of work.
evidence: Four-run comparison report, sanitized archives and bundles, security report, and defect disposition.

work_items.title: Package, document, and release v0
work_items.outcome: Another person can install the CLI and reproduce capture → archive → transfer → verify → resume without private guidance.
work_items.journey: A new user follows the quickstart on a clean supported machine and reproduces the public example within fifteen minutes after installation.
scope: macOS ARM64 and Linux x86_64 release artifacts.
Checksums, signatures, SBOM, compatibility matrix, limitations, public example archive, and migration statement.
acceptance: Clean installation takes under ten minutes.
The quickstart completes in under fifteen minutes after installation.
The public example contains no private or identifying data.
Release checksums, signatures, and SBOM verify.
Entire is documented as the first replaceable provider, not a required future authority.
non_goals: Hosted service availability, federation, CRDT collaboration, or production SLA.
evidence: Release tag and artifacts, clean-machine logs, completed quickstart transcript, and successful offline verification output.
